Marine data arrives in shapes that machine-learning textbooks rarely picture. Depth
profiles, not rows. Tracks with gaps where the tag stopped reporting. Surveys where
the sampling followed the ship and the weather. Species counts where the interesting
species appears in two per cent of hauls.

Preparation is where most of the work happens, and where most of the damage is done.
The damage is usually invisible: a model that scores beautifully because information
leaked from the test set into the training set, and which then fails in the field.

This section works on `coastal-survey-raw.csv`, the same survey used in
[section 1](../01-introduction/index.qmd), but as it came off the ship. It contains
sentinel values, twelve spellings of four substrate types, depths ten times too deep,
duplicate rows, missingness concentrated in winter, a miscalibrated salinity sensor,
and a column computed from the response. All of it is deliberate, and all of it is
ordinary.

::: {.callout-warning}
Leakage is the single most common reason a marine ML result cannot be reproduced in
the field. It reappears in every later section, especially
[7 · Validation](../07-validation/index.qmd).
:::
